summary: The tool entity page covers CanonicalTool, a tool a model may call while it writes, kept as data and never code: a name, a description the model reads, a list of typed fields the model fills in, and one action from a fixed first-party set in src/core/tools.ts. The fields section explains field names, the four types, choices and required flags, and how the function schema and the strict argument check are both made from the one field list so they cannot disagree. The actions section covers roll, which rolls the dice the model writes into a text field, dice, which rolls a linked library dice piece, formula, which runs a linked formula on a copy of the turn's macro context, and record, which only records the call; all four are read-only. The scene section explains how a scene links tools by id in its prompting, the gates they share with the lorebook lookup, how linked tools are read and checked, how call names are made safe and unique, why the same seed rolls the same dice, and that the Control Booth links them, each as a tile with its icon, cost and a switch. Editing describes the tool editor, with its action choice, the shared field editor, and a rail that shows the tool as the AI meets it and tries it. Every connection takes tools except refusing models, and a recognized server refusal is reported in one plain sentence, never retried without tools.

sections.title: Fields
sections.summary: Each field has a name made of a lowercase letter then lowercase letters, digits and underscores, a description, a type of text, number, boolean or choice, and a required flag. Only a choice field carries choices, at least one and unique, and it must carry them. A tool's field names must be unique, and no product limit caps how many fields it has; the names keep the providers' sixty-four character rule. The function schema sent to the model, toolParameters, and the check of the model's arguments, readToolCall, are both built from this one field list, so the two can never disagree. Unknown arguments, missing required arguments, values of the wrong type and choices outside the list are all refused, and the refusal is told to the model.

sections.title: Actions
sections.summary: There are four first-party actions. Roll rolls the dice the model writes into one of the tool's text fields through the dice module, any dice with a die of two or more sides (a long roll is summarised past twenty dice), other text refused when the arguments are read, and the trace keeps each die and the total. Dice rolls a library dice piece by its id, a roll, a table or a pool, answered as that piece rolls. Formula runs a library formula by its id on a copy of the turn's macro context and answers with what it renders; one that would change a variable, has a macro error or is blank is refused, and the refusal is told to the model. Record changes nothing and answers Recorded. All four are read-only.

sections.title: In a scene
sections.summary: A scene links tools by id in its prompting settings, ChatPrompting.tools, in order and without duplicates. They are offered only when Narrator Tool Access is on, the connection takes tools and the turn is not a Continue, the same gates the lorebook lookup uses. Every connection takes tools, local and custom servers included, except a model that refuses them whatever its host. When a server still refuses them, a list of recognized wordings (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM and two generic ones) gives one sentence naming the model and saying to turn off Narrator Tool Access or pick another model; any other refusal shows the server's own error. Nothing is saved as a reply and the turn is never retried without tools. The Story Director reports a recognized refusal as no tool calling, and a Final Cut pass advises tagged mode. library-tools.ts reads each linked tool through strict decoders, call names are made safe and unique, rolls are seeded per turn, and the Control Booth links tools as tiles.

sections.title: Editing
sections.summary: A tool opens in the Workbench's tool editor: the shared header, which says in how many scenes it is linked and lists them on a click, when the AI should use it, a choice of what the tool does (roll a field's dice, roll a dice piece, run a formula, or only note the call), and the fields in the field editor a tracker shares, where a field also says whether the AI must fill it. A piece choice starts with none picked. Renaming the field a roll reads carries the roll from the name the field began with, and deleting it leaves the roll with no field picked. The rail's first tab shows the call name, what it takes as plain lines read off the provider's parameters, and the token cost; its Try tab calls the tool through the real reader and runner and shows exactly the answer the AI would get. A draft the decoder refuses cannot be saved or tried. New tool saves a blank record tool.
